name: Simple Genetic Algorithm
miniText: How do selection and variation search a space of binary strings? NetLogo Simple Genetic Algorithm evolves a population toward the all-ones string, using fitness based on the number of ones, reproduction, crossover, and mutation. Holland [1] supplies the foundational adaptation framework, Mitchell [2] explains representation and genetic operators, and Wolpert and Macready [3] limit claims that any optimizer is universally superior. The display follows the current best string while the population changes between generations. Population size and variation rates alter progress and diversity. The all-ones landscape is intentionally simple and separable; success here does not establish performance on deceptive, noisy, or constrained objectives. Stochastic runs can differ, and selecting a good parent does not guarantee a better child. The model illustrates fitness-driven search under a chosen encoding rather than a complete account of biological evolution.
